issue.title: test_muse_usage_probe_other_host_errors_are_probe_failures reports timeout instead of probe_failed under the loaded full lane

task_type_fields.evidence: Check ToolRun c18076f2e83f97bf91a0a4884ea72732 (2026-11-20, 62327 passed / 2 failed, 65.9s on this node) failed at tests/llm_provider/test_muse_usage_probe.py:310 with "assert 'timeout' == 'probe_failed'": the probe ran in an isolated worker (isolate=True, default deadline) against the fake Muse CLI in mode=usage_read_error, and the whole-probe deadline fired before the fake's usage-read error was classified. The node passed in an isolated rerun on the unchanged tree (0.57s call). Fail rate 1/2; loaded parallel fail, isolated pass. Likely the same shape as closed sase-1k9 (worker and fake-CLI interpreter start-up share one wall clock with the probe deadline), whose fix moved only the missed-mint node in-process. The triggering change (TUI monitor settling lane bucket) does not touch the usage probe.
task_type_fields.repro_cmd: sase tool run check (scoped lane escalated to the full suite under host load)

issue.creation_reason: Failed once in an escalated just check full lane and passed in isolation on the unchanged tree; same load-sensitive deadline class sase-1k9 fixed for a sibling node, but this node was not covered.

payload.description: Closed sibling flake in the same test file with the same load-sensitive probe-deadline shape; its in-process/longer-deadline fix is the likely template
